# Gizmo Warehouse

> Shareable tools, analyses, and work products from Joe Eichenbaum at 17A. A running collection of things built that aren't covered by an NDA.

Joe is a partner at 17A, a consulting firm serving state and local government. Most of his work is confidential; this site is where the shareable residue lives: tools, write-ups, and analyses across public safety, city and state government, healthcare policy, music, and AI.

## Pages

- [Home](/): Browse all gizmos, filterable by category.
- [public safety](/category/public-safety): Category index.
- [music](/category/music): Category index.
- [using ai](/category/using-ai): Category index.
- [city government](/category/city-government): Category index.
- [state government](/category/state-government): Category index.
- [healthcare policy](/category/healthcare-policy): Category index.
- [nyc](/category/nyc): Category index.

## Gizmos

- [Introducing Daf Yomi Dot Dev](/gizmo/daf-yomi) (2026-09): daf-yomi.dev shows today's page of Talmud with a short AI-written note and one question, plus a daily email. How I built it with Claude, and why. Open daf-yomi.dev: https://daf-yomi.dev; Source on GitHub: https://github.com/eichenbaumj/daf-yomi
- [The Only Way to Start Is by Starting](/gizmo/only-way-to-start-is-by-starting) (2026-09): A short whitepaper for agency leaders: one accountable owner, a handful of paid licenses, one real piece of work. The 90-day recipe for AI in government.
- [Music Theory with LLMs](/gizmo/gospel-of-claude-code) (2026-08): I had Claude Code write gospel reharmonizations for my fake book. Why predicting the next chord is a natural job for a language model, with examples. Get the code on GitHub: https://github.com/eichenbaumj/fakebook-maker
- [Pricing the Fear of Data Centers](/gizmo/data-center-restriction-cost) (2026-08): Every documented US data-center restriction on one map, what a town gives up when it says no, and the conditions that beat a ban.
- [The New Math on NYC's Public Grocery Stores](/gizmo/nyc-public-grocery-new-math) (2026-08): NYC's city-owned grocery stores will cut a core basket 30%. A new model prices the hidden subsidy: ~$167M over ten years, reaching ~29,000 New Yorkers a year.
- [High Floor, Low Ceiling: How Public-Sector Wage Compression Erodes Public Service](/gizmo/public-private-compensation-comparison) (2026-06): The public-sector pay gap by skill, state, and over time. Government pay holds up at the bottom of the labor market and falls far behind at the top.
- [These 5 Million People Are About to Lose Their Medicaid — But They Don't Have To](/gizmo/medicaid-work-requirements) (2026-05): Starting Jan 2027, a federal Medicaid work requirement puts 5–10M people at risk. State-by-state model of who's affected and what each state can verify.
- [How to Save the Government from Microsoft Copilot](/gizmo/microsoft-copilot) (2026-05): Why state and local government defaults to Microsoft 365 Copilot, the head-to-head benchmarks against the alternatives, and a one-page AI procurement checklist.
- [NYC Property Tax: Who Pays, Who Doesn't](/gizmo/nyc-property-tax-map) (2026-04): Interactive parcel-level map of NYC effective property-tax rates, with the long answer to why neighbors pay wildly different bills.
- [The Math on NYC's Public Grocery Plan](/gizmo/nyc-public-grocery-math) (2026-04): A 10-year P&L for Mayor Mamdani's five city-owned grocery stores, plus a ranked comparison of what $70M would buy if the goal were feeding more people.
- [Reducing Violent Crime Without New Budget, New Staff, or More Arrests](/gizmo/reducing-violence-whitepaper) (2026-03): Violent crime concentrates on 3 to 5% of a city's blocks. A whitepaper on place-based fixes and cross-department coordination, with Dallas's 2024 to 2025 results.
- [Jazz Fakebook Maker](/gizmo/fakebook-maker) (2026-02): A Python tool that converts plain-text chord charts into a searchable, bookmarked PDF fake book for a laptop on a piano stand. Free code and a public-domain edition. Get the code on GitHub: https://github.com/eichenbaumj/fakebook-maker

## Data pages

One page per state, county, city, or jurisdiction, generated from the datasets behind the pieces above:
- [Data center moratoriums and restrictions by state (2026)](/gizmo/data-center-restriction-cost/tracker): 933 documented local actions and 33 state actions on data centers across 48 states as of August 15, 2026, with a page per state and per jurisdiction.
- [Medicaid work requirements by state: who is subject and who loses coverage (2027)](/gizmo/medicaid-work-requirements/states): State-by-state numbers for the federal Medicaid work requirement starting January 1, 2027: 18,625,071 adults subject nationally, 5,461,400 projected to lose coverage. One page per state with county detail.
- [Public vs private sector pay by state and city (2023)](/gizmo/public-private-compensation-comparison/states): Median and 90th-percentile government vs private hourly wages for 52 states and city-payroll comparisons for 5 cities, from ACS PUMS and payroll files. One page per state and city, by occupation.
